amendments.why: Rule 103's article carve-out is one compressed sentence whose only spelled-out example, LUK.6.30 τὰ σά → *thy goods*, carries no recurring lexeme, while its repeated-predicate-nominal clause spells GAL.3.20 and JAS.3.15 out at length. A verse pass reading the two together took ROM.10.12's ὁ … αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων → *the same Lord is Lord of all* for GAL.3.20's frame and marked the supplied *Lord* `added`, when the word stands inside the article's own phrase and completes it. The amendment names that shape, gives the test that separates the two — whether an article governs the phrase the supplied nominal completes, GAL.3.20's article governing an expressed μεσίτης and so being already complete — and cites rule 102's REV.11.15, where an anaphoric *the kingdom* is folded into the article with βασιλεία expressed in the same verse. Nothing existing is removed or reworded; the corpus rows rule 103 already counts are untouched, and rule 102's fifty-three units agree.
amendments.rule: Supplied English **lexical content whose source token is already realized elsewhere in the verse** is `added` under rule 5, and rule 7 does not fold it. **The test is licensing, not recurrence.** Ask whether some source token's own English expression is still incomplete, not merely whether a same-lexeme English word stands elsewhere in the verse: a supplied word that completes what a token was going to say is a rule 7 helper on it however often that lexeme recurs, and only a word whose licensing token has already spent its English falls here. ACT.10.22 folds the supplied *of God* into `ἐχρηματίσθη`, the lexeme meaning to be divinely instructed, no other token licensing it; LUK.8.23, LUK.8.42 and LUK.8.49 fold *with water*, *of age* and *house* onto the single word whose English they complete; and HEB.6 puts it as present **and unspent** rather than italicized. Where the token that licenses the supplied word is an **article** rather than a spent noun, rule 102 takes it into the article's own phrase and nothing is `added`: `τὰ σά` → *thy goods* gives *goods* to the article at LUK.6.30, and 1CO.15 reads a repetition a substantival article governs the same way. What decides that is **where the supplied nominal stands**, and never which slot the Greek left elliptical: a supplied noun standing inside a phrase a Greek article governs completes that article's own English under rule 102 and is folded there, headed on the supplied noun, however plainly it echoes a noun the same verse expresses elsewhere. `ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων` → *for the same Lord is Lord of all* gives the discontinuous *the … Lord* to the article and a bare *same* to the intensive pronoun, `κύριος` keeping the predicate *is Lord*, exactly as `τοῦ κυρίου` → *the kingdom* does at REV.11.15 with `βασιλεία` standing expressed in the same verse. Where the ASV repeats a predicate nominal the Greek left elliptical, `οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ σοφία ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη` → *This wisdom is not a wisdom that cometh down* marks the second *a wisdom* `added` headed on the nominal, `σοφία` being spent on the first *wisdom*, exactly as `ὁ δὲ μεσίτης ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν` → *a mediator is not a mediator of one* does at GAL.3.20 in the identical frame. GAL.3.20 is that frame and not the one above because its article governs the expressed `μεσίτης`, so the article's phrase is already complete and the repeat stands in a slot no token governs; do not read it as licensing an `added` nominal inside a phrase whose article has no expressed noun of its own. The supplied determiner stays inside the `added` unit, as GAL.3.20, REV.4.1 and REV.20.12 keep it. The corpus reads it this way throughout — a repeated antecedent inside a finite relative rendering at 2CO.3.7, a repeated predicate at REV.17.14 and REV.21.12, a resumed verb at REV.14.14 and 2JN.1.12, and a repeated quantifier at 2PE.3.11 — and 2CO.3.7 says in terms that no unit folds a repeated antecedent after a relativizer. Rule 7's list is *articles, auxiliaries, pronouns, of, to, and similar words*, and a full lexical noun or verb is not among them, which is why the absence of a competitor does not license the fold: a helper belongs to the word that licenses it, and the word that would have licensed this one has already spent its English. A resumptive **pronoun** is the contrast and it goes the other way, being exactly what rule 7 names: `Πολλὰ … γράφειν` → *many things … to write \*them\** folds the *them* onto `Πολλά` at 3JN.1.13. A repeated **function word** is the same contrast and is decided the same way: where one Greek preposition or conjunction governs two coordinate members and the ASV writes its English twice, the second occurrence is a rule 7 helper on the member it introduces and is never `added`, exactly as rule 40 has it for the repeated infinitival marker of `ἵνα ποιήσω … καὶ τελειώσω` → *to do … and to accomplish*, which gives *to accomplish* whole to `τελειώσω`, and as rule 86 already refuses `added` for the English of a conjunction expressed elsewhere in the sentence and repeated in a coordinated clause. `εἰς Μωϋσῆν καὶ τὸν θεόν` → *against Moses and against God* gives the second *against* to `θεόν` under rule 21's determinerless clause and leaves the article `unrepresented`; where the ASV writes a determiner for that member the article carries the repeated preposition instead under rule 21, as it carries any other. Do not stretch the spent preposition over the repetition under rule 15 either: the corpus's `added` units under this rule are nouns, predicates, verbs, quantifiers and antecedents, and not one is a word from rule 7's own list. Rule 11 does not decide this either way, the ASV italicizing such a repetition only sometimes. Rule 37 is the near contrast and is worth ruling out by name, because the two look alike from the English side: there the licensing token stands in a neighbouring verse, whereas here it stands in this one and is already spent. Rule 97 is the other, where the licensing token stands in no verse of the projection at all. Say in the note that reading the repetition as a discontinuous second realization under rule 15 remains defensible, as GAL.3.20, 2CO.3.7 and REV.21.12 each concede.

conventions: A supplied English noun standing inside a phrase a Greek article governs is the article's under rule 102 even where the same lexeme is expressed elsewhere in the verse: ὁ … αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων → *the same Lord is Lord of all* gives the discontinuous *the … Lord* to the article headed on *Lord*, a bare *same* to the intensive pronoun and *is Lord* to κύριος. Rule 103's `added` reading was taken first and is corrected here; GAL.3.20 is not the frame, its article governing an expressed noun. ROM.10.15's τὰ ἀγαθά → *things* and *good* is the same judgment where no lexeme recurs.

*Whosoever* is assigned by which source tokens stand under it, and the chapter writes both cases. At 10:11 πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων gives the one English word to the quantifier and leaves the article `unrepresented` (rule 80). At 10:13 πᾶς ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται gives it to ὃς ἄν as one unit, rule 50 forbidding an `unrepresented` ἄν and rule 80's own clause reserving the `-soever` for a particle standing to answer to it, so πᾶς is `unrepresented` instead. BSB represents πᾶς there; that report is not a correction.

A substantival article before a participle carries its own case preposition — τῶν εὐαγγελιζομένων → *of them* at 10:15, τοῖς … ἐπερωτῶσιν → *unto them* at 10:20 — unless another case-marked source token stands in front of it and the ASV writes the preposition there: παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι → *to every* on the dative quantifier and a bare *one* on the article at 10:4, the article's English being a nominal rather than a determiner for rule 21 to anchor. Where an expressed preposition governs the phrase it keeps its own word and the article stays bare, as ἐν τοῖς … ζητοῦσιν → *of* and *them* at 10:20.

report: Checked all 37 candidate lemma groups, then read the 21 verses end to end for the axis the lemma table cannot see: a supplied English word marked `added` in one verse and folded in another. The chapter carried exactly one `added` unit, and that is where the split is.

ROM.10.15 folds a supplied nominal into the article whose phrase it completes: τὰ ἀγαθά gives *things* to the article and a bare *good* to the adjective (rules 49, 102). ROM.10.12 met the same shape, ὁ … αὐτός → *the same Lord*, and instead marked the supplied *Lord* `added` under rule 103's repeated-predicate-nominal clause, because κύριος is spent on the predicate *is Lord*. Rule 103 says in terms that the test is licensing and not recurrence; its article carve-out (LUK.6.30 τὰ σά → *thy goods*, and the 1CO.15 repetition) with rule 102's REV.11.15 τοῦ κυρίου → *the kingdom*, where βασιλεία stands expressed in the same verse, puts a supplied noun standing inside an article's own phrase with the article. GAL.3.20 is not the identical frame: there the article governs the expressed μεσίτης, so its phrase is already complete and the repeat lands in a slot no token governs.

Patched ROM.10.12 only: ὁ now takes the discontinuous *the … Lord* headed on *Lord*, αὐτός keeps a bare *same*, κύριος keeps *is Lord*, and the chapter has no `added` unit. All 19 source and 26 target ids remain partitioned exactly once. No other verse is touched; nothing else in ROM.10.12 was changed, including the contested τε and *between* edges.

Examined and rejected as splits, each licensed by the source or by what the ASV wrote: *Whosoever* at 10:11 (πᾶς ὁ, rule 80) against 10:13 (πᾶς ὃς ἄν, rule 50 — a particle stands there to take the `-soever`, which rule 80's own clause reserves for it); εἰς σωτηρίαν at 10:1 (recast as a finite purpose clause) against 10:10 (*unto salvation*), each token aligned to its own English; ὁμολογέω heads at 10:9 and 10:10; substantival articles before participles at 10:4, 10:12, 10:15 and 10:20, each split by the count of English words the ASV wrote (rules 32, 90); preverb particles at 10:6, 10:7, 10:18, 10:21, no following preposition's gloss carrying the particle (rule 106); phrasal prepositions kept inside the verb over accusative objects at 10:3, 10:13, 10:14, 10:20; supplied copulas and verbs at 10:1, 10:4, 10:12, 10:15, 10:17 and 10:19, all decided by what is left in the clause to carry them (rules 53, 62, 63, 92); interrogative μή at 10:18 and 10:19 against ordinary μή at 10:6 and 10:20 (rule 44).

BSB: five disagreements, none a genuine error. 10:11 ὁ (rule 80), 10:12 τε (rule 70's one-conjunction arm — only one English conjunction is written for τε … καί, and *between* is a preposition), 10:18 and 10:19 μή (rule 44) are all pre-licensed by the contract as reports that are not corrections. 10:13 πᾶς is not pre-licensed by name, but follows from rule 50's mandate that ἄν never be left `unrepresented` together with rule 80's clause giving the `-soever` to a particle standing to answer to it; the verse note names the competing whole-cluster reading. Nothing was changed to improve the rate.

One amendment returned, to rule 103, naming the ROM.10.12 shape and the test that separates it from GAL.3.20. No new rules: everything else this chapter decided is an application of rules already binding.
